ACTION: Write `specs/2026-10-28-release-notes-breaking-flag-design.md`
```markdown
# Breaking-change flag in release notes

Source: `specs/deferred_items.md`, item 7.

## Goal

Mark breaking changes in the output of `release-notes`.
`announce` lists breaking changes first in its post.
Readers see breaking changes at a glance.

## Context

- `release-notes` writes one bullet for each merged pull request.
- `skills/changelog-check/parse.py` splits each bullet on " — ".
  It rejects a bullet with more than two parts.
- `announce` reads the parsed entries and writes a post.

## Decision

A breaking bullet starts with a `[breaking]` tag:

    - [breaking] <existing bullet text>

A bullet without the tag keeps its current form.

Rejected alternative: a third part, " — breaking: yes".
That option changes the part count that `parse.py` checks.
The tag keeps every untagged bullet valid, so older notes parse as before.

## Changes

1. `skills/release-notes/SKILL.md`: when the pull request has the
   `breaking` label, start its bullet with `[breaking] `.
2. `skills/changelog-check/parse.py`: before the split on " — ",
   remove a leading `[breaking] ` from the bullet text.
   Set `breaking=True` on that entry. Set `breaking=False` on all
   other entries. The two-part rule then applies to the rest of the bullet.
3. `skills/announce/SKILL.md`: list entries with `breaking=True` first.
   Keep the existing order inside each group.

## Tag rules

- The tag matches only at the start of the bullet text, after "- ".
- The match is exact and lowercase: `[breaking]`.
- A `[breaking]` string at another position is ordinary text.

## Tests

In `skills/changelog-check/`:

1. A tagged bullet parses with `breaking=True` and the same fields as
   the bullet without its tag.
2. An untagged bullet parses with `breaking=False` and the same fields as before.

## Out of scope

- No change to existing release notes. No backfill of the tag.
- No other labels or tags.
```

The spec is at `specs/2026-10-28-release-notes-breaking-flag-design.md`. Please review it before I write the implementation plan.

I added two rules that we did not discuss. Please check them:

- **Tag position.** `[breaking]` counts only at the start of the bullet. In any other position it is ordinary text. A pull-request title that contains the word "[breaking]" will therefore not flag the bullet by accident.
- **Exact match.** The tag is lowercase `[breaking]`. `[Breaking]` is not a tag. I chose this to keep `parse.py` strict, like its two-part rule.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The tag comes off *before* the " — " split. Because of this, the two-part check in `parse.py` does not change. The new field cannot weaken the old validation.
- `announce` is a skill, so its change is an instruction in `SKILL.md`, not code. Only `parse.py` gets a unit test. The `announce` ordering is tested only when someone runs the skill.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

When you approve the spec, the next step is the `writing-plans` skill. Your routing rules put planning on Opus and execution on Sonnet. So after the plan is written, start a fresh Sonnet session (`claude --model sonnet`) and give it the plan file.
